I want to create a toy car model. Create a box with dimensions 200x100x100(X,Y,Z) as the body. The windshield can be created by subtracting a 50x100x50 block from an upper edge of the box. Add four wheels with a radius of 25 and a thickness of 10: Place two at (25,0,0) and (175,0,0) facing in the Y-Axis (0,1,0), and two at (25,100,0) and (175,100,0) facing in the negative Y-Axis (0,-1,0). | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step plan (no function calls executed yet)

1  Body  
• Start the model with one rectangular block that represents the car body.  
• Give the block the full requested dimensions 200 × 100 × 100 (X, Y, Z).  
• Place its base point at the global origin (0, 0, 0) so it extends to (200, 100, 100).  
• This first block is the additive “seed”, so subtraction = False.

2  Windshield cut-out  
• Create another block 50 × 100 × 50 to carve the windshield.  
• Position its base point at (150, 0, 50):  
  – X = 150 so it occupies the front-most 50 mm of the body (150 → 200).  
  – Y = 0 so it spans the full width (0 → 100).  
  – Z = 50 so it removes only the upper half (50 → 100).  
• Mark this block as a subtraction volume (subtraction = True).

3  Wheels (4 cylinders)  
All wheels have radius = 25 mm and length (thickness) = 10 mm.

a) Front-left wheel  
• Base center (25, 0, 0)  
• Axis vector (0, 10, 0)  → points in +Y, length = 10.  
• subtraction = False.

b) Front-right wheel  
• Base center (175, 0, 0)  
• Axis vector (0, 10, 0)  
• subtraction = False.

c) Rear-left wheel  
• Base center (25, 100, 0)  
• Axis vector (0, -10, 0)  → points in ‑Y, length = 10.  
• subtraction = False.

d) Rear-right wheel  
• Base center (175, 100, 0)  
• Axis vector (0, -10, 0)  
• subtraction = False.

4  Order of operations  
• Call block() once for the body (additive).  
• Call block() again for the windshield (subtractive).  
• Call cylinder() four times for the wheels (additive).  
• Finally call finished() with allFunctionsCalled = True.

Let me know when you want me to prepare the actual function-call bundle in executable form.
